Summary: The pain I have right now is giving secrets to the places that do my work: vault keys to a browser where the passkey does not reach, and vault keys to the agent sessions I schedule every day. Copying them by hand is slow and risky, and when I tell an agent in its prompt that something is a secret to be careful with, it sometimes refuses to use it at all. So I wantwould like SG/Send's technology to focus on one use case: handing a secret, or a public key, to an agent or a browser, as a separate site, mostly client-side, with a command line. The back end already has most of what this needs: a transfer that can be downloaded once and then deleted, an expiry, and client-side encryption; it does not, I found, restrict by location, which I thought it did. The design flips the usual direction: the recipient makes its own key pair where it runs and shows only the public half, by QR code, link or paste; the owner encrypts the secret to it and signs it; the drop is read once; and the secret goes from the drop into the tool, never into the chat. This site's agent ran it end to end on a local server: the agent decrypted the secret, the second download got a 410, the owner's signature verified once the agent knew the owner's key, and a browser made a key pair it refused to export. The industry is moving the other way, keeping secrets out of agents entirely; for an encrypted vault that cannot work, because the key has to reach the place that decrypts.
